butir.teks: As for the verses, there is the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: ⟦QS 9:122⟧ What is meant is teaching and guidance.
And the saying of Allah Most High: ⟦QS 3:187⟧ This is an obligation to teach.

And the saying of Allah Most High: ⟦QS 2:146⟧ This is a prohibition of concealment, just as He, Most High, said regarding testimony: ⟦QS 2:283⟧ The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Allah has never given a scholar knowledge without taking from him the covenant He took from the prophets: that they make it clear to the people and not conceal it." (٦) And Allah Most High said: ⟦QS 41:33⟧ And Allah Most High said: ⟦QS 16:125⟧ And Allah Most High said: ⟦QS 2:129⟧ As for the reports, there is his saying (peace and blessings be upon him) when he sent Mu'adh (may Allah be pleased with him) to Yemen: "That Allah should guide a single man through you is better for you than this world and all that is in it."

The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Whoever learns a chapter of knowledge in order to teach people is given the reward of seventy truthful ones (siddiq)." (١) And Jesus (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Whoever knows, acts, and teaches is called great in the kingdom of the heavens."

The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, Allah, glorified is He, will say to the worshippers and to those who strive, 'Enter Paradise.' Then the scholars will say, 'It was by the merit of our knowledge that they worshipped and strove.' So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will say, 'You are to Me like some of My angels. Intercede, and your intercession will be accepted.' So they intercede, and then they enter Paradise." (٢) And this applies only to knowledge that extends to others through teaching, not to knowledge that stays confined and does not extend.

The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, does not snatch knowledge away from people after having given it to them. Rather, it departs with the departure of the scholars. Whenever a scholar departs, he takes with him the knowledge he had, until, when none remain except ignorant leaders who give legal rulings without knowledge when they are asked, they go astray and lead others astray." (٣) And he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Whoever knows something and conceals it, Allah will bridle him on the Day of Resurrection with a bridle of fire." (٤) And he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "What an excellent gift and what an excellent present: a word of wisdom that you hear and hold on to, then carry to a Muslim brother of yours and teach him; it equals a year of worship." (٥) And he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "This world is cursed, and everything in it is cursed, except the remembrance of Allah, glorified is He, and what is connected with it, or a teacher or a learner." (٦) And he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Allah, glorified is He, and His angels, and the inhabitants of His heavens and His earth, even the ant in its hole and even the fish in the sea, send blessings upon the one who teaches people good." (٧) And he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "A Muslim has never given his brother a benefit better than a good hadith that reached him and that he then passed on." (٨) And he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "A word of good that a believer hears, then teaches and acts upon, is better for him than a year of worship." (٩) And the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) went out one day and saw two gatherings. In one of them they were calling on Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and beseeching Him, and in the other they were teaching people. He said: "As for these, they are asking Allah Most High; if He wills, He gives them, and if He wills, He withholds. As for those, they are teaching people, and I was sent only as a teacher." Then he turned to them and sat with them. (١٠) And he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "The likeness of what Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, sent me with of guidance and knowledge is that of abundant rain that fell upon a land. Part of it was a patch that received the water and grew abundant herbage and grass. Part of it was a patch that held the water, and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, benefited people with it, so they drank from it, gave their animals water, and sowed crops. And part of it was barren flats that neither held water nor grew herbage." (١١) End. The first he gave as a likeness of one who benefits from his knowledge, the second as a likeness of one who gives benefit, and the third as a likeness of one deprived of both.

The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "When the son of Adam dies, his deeds come to an end except for three: knowledge that is benefited from..." and the rest of the hadith. (١) And he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "The one who points to good is like the one who does it." (٢) And he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "There is no envy except in two: a man to whom Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has given wisdom, so he judges by it and teaches it to people, and a man to whom Allah has given wealth and whom He has empowered to exhaust it in good." (٣) And he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Upon my successors is the mercy of Allah." It was asked, "And who are your successors?" He said: "Those who revive my Sunna and teach it to the servants of Allah." (٤) As for the reports (athar), 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "Whoever relates a hadith and it is then acted upon will have a reward like that of the one who acts on it."
Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: "Everything asks forgiveness for the one who teaches people good, even the fish in the sea."
Some of the scholars said: "The scholar enters into what lies between Allah and His creation, so let him consider how he enters."

It is reported that Sufyan ath-Thawri (may Allah have mercy on him) came to Asqalan and stayed there while no one asked him anything. He said: "Hire a mount for me so that I may leave this town; this is a town in which knowledge dies."

He said that only out of eagerness for the merit of teaching and for keeping knowledge alive through it. 'Ata' (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "I went in to Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib while he was weeping, and I said, 'What makes you weep?' He said, 'No one asks me about anything.'" And some of them said: "The scholars are the lamps of the ages; each one is the lantern of his time, by which the people of his era are illuminated."

Al-Hasan (may Allah have mercy on him) said: "Were it not for the scholars, people would become like beasts." That is, through teaching they bring people out of the bounds of animality into the bounds of humanity.
'Ikrima said: "This knowledge has a price." It was asked, "And what is it?" He said: "That you place it with someone who carries it well and does not waste it."

Yahya ibn Mu'adh said: "The scholars are more merciful to the community of Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon him) than their own fathers and mothers." It was asked, "How is that?" He said: "Because their fathers and mothers protect them from the fire of this world, while the scholars protect them from the fire of the Hereafter."
It was said: "The beginning of knowledge is silence, then listening, then memorizing, then acting, then spreading it."

It was said: "Teach your knowledge to the one who is ignorant, and learn from the one who knows what you do not know. For if you do that, you will come to know what you did not know, and you will preserve what you know."

Mu'adh ibn Jabal said, concerning teaching and learning, and I have also seen it as raised (marfu'): "Learn knowledge, for learning it for Allah's sake is reverential fear, seeking it is worship, studying it together is glorification, searching into it is jihad, teaching it to one who does not know it is charity, and devoting it to those who deserve it is an act of drawing near to Allah. It is the intimate companion in loneliness and the friend in solitude. It is the guide to the religion, what gives patience in ease and in hardship, the minister among close friends, the kinsman among strangers, and the beacon on the path to Paradise. By it Allah raises peoples and makes them, in what is good, leaders, masters, and guides who are followed, guides to good whose footsteps are traced and whose deeds are watched. The angels long for their friendship and stroke them with their wings, and everything moist and dry asks forgiveness for them, even the fish of the sea and its creeping things, the beasts of prey of the land and its cattle, and the sky and its stars. (٥) For knowledge is the life of hearts from blindness, the light of eyes from darkness, and the strength of bodies from weakness. By it the servant reaches the stations of the righteous and the highest ranks. Reflection upon it is equal to fasting, and studying it together is equal to night prayer. By it Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is obeyed; by it He is worshipped; by it He is affirmed as One; by it He is glorified; by it scrupulousness (wara') is practiced; by it ties of kinship are maintained; and by it the lawful and the forbidden are known. It is the leader, and action is its follower. The fortunate are inspired with it, and the wretched are deprived of it." We ask Allah Most High for good success.
